name: Castleford Rangers

location.about: A town of about 95,000 eleven miles down the River Wick from Northwick, where the Wick meets the Aire. Coal and glass made it: the pits ringed the town and the great glassworks by the river blew bottles for half the country. The last pit closed in 1986 and the glassworks in 2002, but the furnace chimney still stands by the river - and the football club is still called the Glassmen.

colours.story: Royal blue for the glassworks' famous blue bottles, and white sleeves since 1921 - the year of the first title - when the captain, Harold Pickersgill, cut the sleeves off his shirt in a heatwave and the club made it the kit.

home.shirt: royal blue with white sleeves and a white collar

away.shirt: amber with a navy collar and navy cuffs

rivals.why: the big city eleven miles up the Wick - first played in 1873, older than the League itself; Northwick have the money and the trophies, Castleford have the grudge
the 1966 title race, won on the last day at Kingsmere, and a run of bad-tempered cup ties in the eighties

history.title: Glassblowers and pitmen
history.text: Founded in 1872 by workers from the riverside glassworks and the Wheldale pit. The first West Riding Derby, against Northwick in 1873, was abandoned when the crowd came onto the pitch - a tradition, some say, that has never quite died.

history.title: Always second
history.text: League runners-up in 1892, 1898, 1899 and 1903 - four times the bridesmaid in twelve years. Moved to Wickside, on the river bank by the glassworks, in 1901.

history.title: The first titles
history.text: Champions at last in 1921, the year of Harold Pickersgill's white sleeves, and again in 1931. Second in 1922, 1925, 1930 and 1937 - and the Association Cup in 1937.

history.title: Down and back
history.text: Relegated for the only time in their first-class history in 1949. Back up as Second Division champions in 1952, and second again in 1963 with a young side built by Bill Shackleton.

history.title: Shackleton's champions
history.text: Bill Shackleton's team won the title in 1966 on the last day, at Kingsmere. Champions again in 1979 - a point ahead of Northwick, the sweetest of them all - and in 1983, with the Association Cup in 1984 and 1986 and the League Cup in 1989.

history.title: Wickside reborn
history.text: Wickside was rebuilt through the nineties. Champions in 2001, runners-up three seasons running from 2004, and in 2006 the best year in the club's history: the Continental Champions' Cup, the World Club Trophy, the Association Cup and the League Cup.

history.title: Still standing
history.text: Titles in 2011 and 2017, the Association Cup in 2020 and the League Cup in 2021. Northwick are bigger and richer, but Castleford have beaten them to the title three times - and the town reminds them every derby day.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1921 = 1920-21).

legends.name: Bill Shackleton
legends.note: Three titles and the 1984 Association Cup. The Shackleton Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Harold Pickersgill
legends.note: Captain of the first title side - and the man behind the white sleeves.

legends.name: Gareth Hollis
legends.note: Two titles and the 2006 Continental Champions' Cup.

legends.name: Marco Di Salvo
legends.note: Scored twice in the 2006 Champions' Cup final.

badge.about: The glassworks' furnace chimney and a blue glass bottle for the town's trade; the crossed picks for the pits; the white rose for Yorkshire; 1872 for the year. Motto 'Ex Igne Lux' - out of the fire, light.
badge.design: A royal-blue roundel with a thin white border. In the centre, a white glassworks chimney with a curl of white smoke, and in front of it a blue glass bottle outlined in white. Two crossed white miner's picks behind the chimney. A small white Yorkshire rose at the top. '1872' in white at the bottom. 'CASTLEFORD RANGERS' in white capitals around the ring, and a white ribbon beneath reading 'EX IGNE LUX' in blue.

ground.name: Wickside

stands.name: Shackleton Stand
stands.features: the main stand: dressing rooms, tunnel and dugouts on the halfway line, boxes between the tiers; Bill Shackleton's statue outside

stands.name: Glassworks End
stands.roof: cantilever with a steep white truss
stands.features: the home end - one huge steep single tier, the old kop rebuilt with seats; the glassworks' brick furnace chimney stands right behind it by the river; a giant 'EX IGNE LUX' flag

stands.name: East Stand
stands.roof: 1970s cantilever on a big steel frame
stands.features: two tiers under a big 1970s cantilever roof, starting to show its age; family section in the lower tier; the River Wick and the old towpath right behind it

stands.name: Aire Road End
stands.features: away fans in the upper tier; the big screen in the corner

ground.corners: the two northern corners filled in with seats (2004); the southern corners open
ground.roof: four separate cantilever roofs, the East Stand's older and lower
ground.surroundings: the River Wick along the east side, the glassworks' furnace chimney and old brick sheds behind the Glassworks End, terraced streets and a rugby ground to the south, the green-capped spoil heaps of the old pits on the skyline
ground.atmosphere: the Glassworks End is one of the loudest home ends in the country; derby days against Northwick are ferocious

for_the_engine.notes: a standard-sized pitch; a big, steep home end
